questions.text:
Consider the minterm list form of a Boolean function F given below.
[latex]F(P,Q,R,S)=\sum m(0,2,5,7,9,11)+d(3,8,10,12,14)[/latex]
Here, m denotes a minterm and d denotes a don't care term. The number of essential prime implicants of the function F is ______.
questions.solution:
Prime implicants that are forced:
- 0 can only be covered by [latex]\bar Q\bar S[/latex] (0, 2, 8, 10) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] essential
- 5 can only be covered by [latex]\bar PQS[/latex] (5, 7) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] essential
- 9 can only be covered by [latex]P\bar Q[/latex] (8, 9, 10, 11) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] essential

These three already cover all minterms.

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Consider the unsigned 8-bit fixed point binary Number System below,

[latex]b_7 b_6 b_5 b_4 b_3 . b_2 b_1 b_0[/latex]

where the position of the binary point is between [latex]b_3 \; and \; b_2[/latex]. Assume [latex]b_7[/latex] is the most significant bit. Some of the decimal numbers listed below cannot be represented exactly in the above representation:

(i) 31.500 (ii) 0.875 (iii) 12.100 (iv) 3.001

Which one of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
5 integer bits and 3 fraction bits: representable values are multiples of 1/8 = 0.125 from 0 to 31.875.
- 31.5 True, 0.875 = 7/8 True
- 12.1 and 3.001 are not multiples of 1/8 False

Answer: Only (iii) and (iv) cannot be exactly represented

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: None of (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) can be exactly represented
Only (iii) and (iv) cannot be exactly represented
Only (i) and (ii) cannot be exactly represented

questions.text:
Consider the sequential circuit shown in the figure, where both flip-flops used are positive edge-triggered D flip-flops.

The number of states in the state transition diagram of this circuit that have a transition back to the same state on some value of "in" is _____.
questions.solution:
The two D flip-flops form a shift register: next state ([latex]Q_1,Q_2[/latex]) = (in, [latex]Q_1[/latex]). A state goes back to itself only if in = [latex]Q_1[/latex] = [latex]Q_2[/latex]: state 00 (with in = 0) and state 11 (with in = 1).

Answer: 2

questions.text: Let [latex]\bigoplus[/latex] and [latex]\bigodot[/latex] denote the Exclusive OR and Exclusive NOR operations, respectively. Which one of the following is NOT CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Check option 4: [latex]P\oplus\bar P=1[/latex], so the left side is [latex]1\oplus Q=\bar Q[/latex]. [latex]P\odot\bar P=0[/latex], so the right side is [latex]0\odot\bar Q=\overline{0\oplus\bar Q}=Q[/latex]. [latex]\bar Q\ne Q[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not correct.

Options 1-3 are standard identities.

Answer: Option 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Octal to binary: 1 2 1 7 = 001 010 001 111. Regroup in 4s: 0010 1000 1111 = 2 8 F.

Answer: (028F)16
